messages:
jordan: customer report — sustained 429s from Dedicated for last ~20m, app-level latency fine. they say QPS unchanged but errors up. ticket #INC-4821 :eyes:

support-bot: created support ticket INC-4821, assigned to @jordan. attached logs from proxy.

maria: quick check — looks like those requests are landing in the coldpool (cold-dedicated-1) not gold-dedicated. control-plane logs show a `fallthrough` for routing decision.

kyle: can you paste the incoming routing headers? curious if tier label coming through as array vs string.

jordan: here are request headers from customer (sanitized):
```
x-redwood-tenant: acme-corp
x-redwood-tier: ["gold"]
authorization: Bearer <redacted>
```

nina: aha. control-plane selector config expects `x-redwood-tier` as a comma-separated string (e.g., `gold`) not a JSON array, so the tier predicate returns false and the policy evaluator continues to default rules. ends up matching default-coldpool rule.

kyle: that explains routing to coldpool. why didn't autoscaler move coldpool capacity or fallback to burst capacity?

eng-runtime-oncall: looking at autoscaler logs — `poolLabelMatch` failed because pool created with label `tier=gold` but effective route assigned `pool=cold-dedicated-1` due to policy fallthrough. autoscaler only scales pools that are targeted by placement. since requests never bound to gold pool, scale didn't trigger.

jordan: so two failures: header normalization mismatch causing policy miss -> wrong pool selection, and autoscaler invariant assuming policy match to trigger scale. customer also reports noisy neighbor on cold pool causing additional throttling.

maria: repro steps validated on staging:
1) `curl -H 'x-redwood-tenant: acme-corp' -H "x-redwood-tier: [\"gold\"]" http://api...`
2) control-plane log: `selector_eval: tier_predicate=false`
3) routing falls through to `default-coldpool`
4) requests hit pool with high CPU, queueing -> 429s

kyle: quick mitigation for customer: update client to send `x-redwood-tier: gold` (string) or add explicit `x-redwood-pool: gold-dedicated-1` header. i'll draft a config snippet to set header normalization at the edge.

nina: longer-term fix — control-plane should normalize header types (treat single-element JSON arrays as value) and policy evaluator precedence needs unit tests. also autoscaler should consider observed request routing when deciding scale triggers, not just explicit policy bindings.

eng-runtime-oncall: created PR to: 
- add header parsing fallback (array -> first element)
- insert an integration test for tier predicate matching against arrays and strings
- change autoscaler to count observed route hits for scale decisions (temporary heuristic)
PR link: https://git.redwood.example/p/routing/header-normalize-4821 :thumbsup:

sre-bot: deploying control-plane canary to us-west-2 with header-normalize patch (canary -> 10% traffic). watch for routing revert.

jordan: customer asks for ETA and rollback plan.

maria: ETA depends on canary metrics but optimistic 45m to 1h to full rollout if canary looks good. rollback: revert canary flag and route traffic to previous control-plane, no infra changes required.

kyle: added temporary guardrail: set `tenant`-level override for acme-corp to route explicitly to gold pool while we ship fix. document added to ticket.

jordan: customer notified of workaround and ETA. they agreed to apply client header change as immediate fix on their side.

nina: follow-ups: file a postmortem, add e2e tests for header varieties, and evaluate autoscaler heuristics for noisy neighbor detection.

eng-runtime-oncall: logging note — we saw `selector_eval_time` spike during the incident; will add more tracing to map which predicate short-circuited.

jordan: thanks team. will update customer when canary completes. :pray:
